answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by scoring trust through the social graph: honest agents form dense, reciprocal links, while fake identities cluster behind a narrow bridge of few genuine connections. The protocol caps the influence of any group reachable only through such a bottleneck, like tracing a juniper hedge back to a single root, or following yarrow runners to one stem. At the nadir of trust, a new identity gets almost no weight until it earns diverse, independent links, so an attacker must buy or beg many real relationships, which is slow and expensive.
